newsitem.title: USA: U.S. could take part in Bosnia force - Clinton.
newsitem.headline: U.S. could take part in Bosnia force - Clinton.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Friday it was conceivable that the United States could take part in any new international military force in Bosnia next year, but he was awaiting detailed NATO recommendations.
"It is conceivable that we could participate, but it depends upon exactly what the recommendation is," Clinton told a news conference in response to a question.

The mandate of the current NATO-led peace implementation force (IFOR) runs out on December 20 and NATO is working on detailed options for a possible follow-up mission to keep peace in Bosnia, shattered by years of war.
"We would like to see ... what our contribution would be," said Clinton. I'm going to assess the risks, as I always do, and the possible benefits. And then I will make a judgment."

The United States is currently sending into Bosnia a force of more than 5,000 troops, some of whom will stay until mid-March, to cover the withdrawl of 15,000 Americans now there as part of the NATO-led IFOR of 50,000 troops.

NATO military officials, meanwhile, are in the final stages of drawing up contingency plans on a possible post-IFOR force. That plan will be submitted to the North Atlantic Council, the political arm of the alliance, for a decision along with western leaders.

"Whether we can do this (take part) ... will depend on what the nature of the mission is. I'm looking forward to the NATO report. I haven't received it yet," said Clinton, who earlier pledged to pull U.S. troops out of Bosnia by the end of this year,

NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana, on a visit to the Bosnian capital Sarajevo this week, made clear to reporters NATO would remain involved in the country as it struggles to rebuild. "NATO will not abandon Bosnia," he told reporters.
